questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: In a person on a high potassium diet, which part of the nephron would be expected to secrete the most potassium?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Collecting tubule Potassium secretion occurs in the late DCT and collecting tubules. A high potassium diet will increase the aldosterone levels which in turn increases secretion from the late DCT and CT.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which nephron segment is the primary site of magnesium reabsorption in normal conditions?

options.label: B
options.text: Descending thin segment of loop of henle

options.label: C
options.text: Thick ascending limb of loop of henle

questions.answerText: Thick ascending limb of loop of henle
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Thick ascending limb of loop of henle The primary site of magnesium reabsorption is the TAL, where 65% of the filtered magnesium is reabsorbed. The PCT normally reabsorbs only about 25% of the filtered magnesium, and the DCT and CT reabsorb less than 5%.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: A 55-year old male has renovascular hypertension as a result of renal artery stenosis of left kidney. Which of the following is an unlikely finding in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Increased renal afferent arteriolar pressure Renal artery stenosis results in a decreased renal afferent arteriolar pressure which in turn results in increased release of renin, increased angiotensin II and aldosterone.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following has the highest clearance?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) PAH in low concentration (<20mg/dL) is freely filtered and completely secreted in the PCT and therefore, has a very high clearance. At high concentrations there is incomplete secretion of PAH which decreases its clearance.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Tubular concentration of which of the following substances will be the highest at the end of PCT?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) PAH PAH is freely filtered and completely secreted in the PCT. Its tubular fluid concentration will therefore, be the highest at the end of PCT.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stemHtml: Which set of changes would be expected to occur in response to direct increases in renal arterial pressure without an intact tubuloglomerular feedback system?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) If there is increase in renal arterial pressure, normally GFR tends to remain unchanged because of mainly the tubuloglomerular feedback mechanism. However, in the absence of TGF, an important renal autoregulatory mechanism, increase in renal arterial pressure will result in a significant increase in GFR, sodium and water excretion.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: A patient has a GFR of 100mL/min, urine flow rate of 2mL/min and a plasma glucose concentration of 200mg/dL. If the TmG (transport maxima for Glucose) is 250mg/min, what would be this patient’s rate of glucose excretion?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) 0mg/min Filtered rate of glucose (mg/min) = GFR (mL/min) X plasma glucose (mg/mL) = 100 X 2 = 200mg/min The TmG is 250mg/min. Since the filtered rate of glucose is less than the TmG, all of the filtered glucose will be reabsorbed and there is no glucose in urine.
questions.stemHtml: A patient has a GFR of 100mL/min, urine flow rate of 2mL/min and a plasma glucose concentration of 200mg/dL. If the TmG (transport maxima for Glucose) is 250mg/min, what would be this patient’s rate of glucose excretion?

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: At which site in the nephron will the concentration of creatinine be the highest in a normally hydrated person?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) CD Creatinine is freely filtered, not reabsorbed and only slightly secreted. As there is no reabsorption of creatinine in the tubule the tubular concentration of creatinine progressively increases as water is reabsorbed.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stemHtml: Given below are the renal clearance curves for different substances If C is renal clearance of Inulin, curve D corresponds to renal clearance of which of the following substances?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Glucose Below renal threshold (2mg/mL), clearance of glucose is zero. As the plasma concentration of glucose increases, its clearance also increases and approaches the clearance of inulin but is always less than the clearance of inulin. This is because there will always be some reabsorption of inulin.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following substances has the highest TF/P ratios at the end of the PCT?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

PAH

PAH is freely filtered and completely secreted in the PCT. Its tubular fluid concentration will therefore, be the highest at the end of PCT.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: All of the following increase GFR except?

options.label: A
options.text: Increase in glomerular capillary ultrafiltration coefficient

options.label: B
options.text: Increase in glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure

options.label: C
options.text: Increase in glomerular capillary colloid osmotic pressure

questions.answerText: Increase in glomerular capillary colloid osmotic pressure
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Increase in glomerular capillary colloid osmotic pressure The forces which favour filtration in glomerular capillaries are:- • Glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure • Bowman’s capsule colloid osmotic pressure Increase in forces favouring filtration will increase GFR. Forces which oppose filtration in glomerular capillaries are • Glomerular capillary colloid osmotic pressure • Bowman’s capsule hydrostatic pressure Increase in forces which oppose filtration will decrease GFR. Glomerular capillary ultrafiltration coefficient is a product of glomerular capillary permeability and surface area. Increase in either or both will increase the filtration coefficient and increase GFR. Mesangial cell relaxation will increase surface area available for filtration increasing GFR.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: In conditions associated with very high ADH secretion, such as dehydration, maximum water reabsorption occurs in which of the following segments of the nephron?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) PCT Whether ADH secretion is high or low maximum water reabsorption occurs in the PCT. Two-thirds of the filtered water is reabsorbed in the PCT- this is k/a obligatory water reabsorption.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Sensor for tubuloglomerular feedback is which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Macula densa cells Macula densa cells, which are modified tubular epithelial cells at the beginning of DCT, are a sensor for tubule glomerular feedback.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Acidification of the urine occurs in which of the following segments of the nephron?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Though the maximum secretion of H+ occurs in the PCT, acidification of urine occurs in the late DCT and CD.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: All of the following cause a mesangial cell contraction except
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) The following cause a mesangial cell contraction:- • Endothelin • Angiotensin II • Vasopressin • Noe epinephrine • Platelet activating factor • Platelet derived growth factor • Thromboxane A2 • PGF2 • Leukotrienes C4 and D4 • Histamine The following cause a mesangial cell relaxation :- • ANP • Dopamine • PGE2 • cAMP Mesangial cell contraction causes “kinking” of glomerular capillaries, decreasing the surface area available for filtration, decreasing Kf (Kf = permeability X surface area) and therefore, GFR.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: A high potassium diet is most likely to produce which of the following changes?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Increase in plasma levels of potassium is a potent stimulus for release of aldosterone.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following acquaporins is involved in water reabsorption from the PCT?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Acquaporin 1 is present on both the apical and basolateral membrane of the cells of the PCT. Water reabsorption in the PCT is solute driven and follows the osmotic gradient set up by the active transport of solutes, and isotonicity is maintained.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: If the average hydrostatic pressure in the glomerular capillaries is 50 mm Hg, the hydrostatic pressure in the Bowman’s space is 12 mm Hg, the average colloid osmotic pressure in the glomerular capillaries is 30 mm Hg, and there is no protein in the glomerular ultrafiltrate, what is the net pressure driving glomerular filtration?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) 8 mm Hg Since there are no proteins in the glomerular filtrate, the colloid osmotic pressure in the Bowman’s space is 0. Net filtration pressure = PGC – πGC – PBC + πBC = 50 – 30 – 12 + 0 = 8 mm Hg

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Calculate the rate of potassium excretion from the following data Creatinine clearance = 90mL/min Plasma K+ = 4mEq/ L Urine K+= 60mEq/ L Urine flow rate = 1mL/ min
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) 0.06 mEq/min Filtration rate = Urine flow rate (mL/min) X Urinary concentration of that substance (mEq/mL) Filtration rate of K+= Urine flow rate (mL/min) X urinary K+concentration (mEq/mL) = 1 mL/min X 0.06 mEq/mL = 0.06 mEq/min

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: The maximum clearance rate possible for a substance that is totally cleared from the plasma is equal to which of the following?

options.label: C
options.text: Urinary excretion rate of that substance

questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Renal plasma flow A substance that is freely filtered and completely secreted (eg., PAH at low concentration) is totally cleared from the plasma. The clearance rate of such a substance will be equal to the renal plasma flow.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which changes would you expect to find after administration of a vasodilator drug that caused a 50% decrease in afferent arteriolar resistance and no change in arterial pressure?

options.label: A
options.text: Decreased renal blood flow, decreased glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure

options.label: B
options.text: Increased renal blood flow, increased glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure

options.label: C
options.text: Decreased renal blood flow, increased glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure

options.label: D
options.text: Increased renal blood flow, decreased glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure

questions.answerText: Increased renal blood flow, increased glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Increased renal blood flow, Increased glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure A reduction in the renal afferent arteriolar resistance will increase the renal blood flow. More the flow into the glomerular capillaries, more will be the glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: The GFR of a 50-year-old man decreases by 50% and remains at that level. Plasma concentration of which of the following substances will be increased to the greatest extent?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Creatinine Creatinine is freely filtered, not reabsorbed and slightly secreted. Excretion of creatinine is, therefore, dependent almost entirely on glomerular filtration. A decrease in GFR will therefore, cause the greatest increase in plasma concentration of creatinine. Plasma concentrations of glucose, potassium and sodium are closely regulated by multiple mechanisms that keep them relatively constant even when the GFR falls to very low levels.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stemHtml: The graph given below depicts filterability of dextran through the kidney, 1 representing complete filtration and 0 representing no filtration. Which of the following are A, B and C respectively?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Polycationic, neutral, polyanionic Since the basement membrane of the glomerular filtration membrane has a negative charge, anionic substances will have the least filterability. The relative filterability of dextrans of the same molecular weights will be maximum for polycationic dextrans, followed by neutral dextrans and least for polyanionic dextrans.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following will occur in a dehydrated person deprived of water for more than 24 hours?

options.label: D
options.text: Increased water permeability in the collecting ducts

questions.answerText: Increased water permeability in the collecting ducts
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Increased water permeability in the collecting ducts In a dehydrated person, increased plasma osmolality and decreased ECF volume will result in increased ADH secretion. ADH increases the insertion of acquporin 2 in the luminal membrane of cells of the collecting duct increasing their permeability to water and therefore, increasing the water reabsorption. Decreased ECF volume increases the plasma renin activity, increases ADH but decreases ANP.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the tubular fluid that passes through the lumen of the early distal tubule in the region of the macula densa?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) It is usually hypotonic Fluid entering the early distal tubule is almost always hypotonic. This is because water is reabsorbed in the DTS and electrolytes are reabsorbed in the TAL but the reabsorption of Na+, K+, Cl- in TAL is more than the reabsorption of water in the DTS, making the tubular fluid dilute.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following decreases in length during a muscle contraction?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) I band of sarcomere During a muscle contraction the I band of sarcomere slides into the A band, reducing the length of I band.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Motor end plate potential at neuro- muscular junctions is mainly due to which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: Sodium influx through voltage-gated sodium channels

options.label: B
options.text: Sodium influx through ligand-gated sodium channels

options.label: C
options.text: Potassium efflux through voltage-gated potassium channels

options.label: D
options.text: Potassium efflux through ligand-gated potassium channels

questions.answerText: Sodium influx through ligand-gated sodium channels
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Sodium influx through ligand-gated sodium channels Ach exocytosed by the ending of the Aα motor neuron diffuses across the synaptic cleft to bind with Ach receptors. The Ach receptors are ligand-gated sodium and potassium channels. The movement of sodium predominates resulting in a motor end plate potential. These local potentials generated at the motor end plate summate and an action potential is generated by opening of voltage gated sodium channels. This action potential travels all over the muscle fibre membrane.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following statements comparing fast-twitch and slow-twitch muscle fibres is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Fast-twitch muscle fibres are more dependent on the phosphagen and glycogen- lactic acid systems

options.label: B
options.text: Fast-twitch muscle fibres have more myoglobin

options.label: C
options.text: Fewer capillaries surround slow-twitch muscle fibres

options.label: D
options.text: Fast twitch muscle fibres are smaller in diameter

questions.answerText: Fast-twitch muscle fibres are more dependent on the phosphagen and glycogen- lactic acid systems
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Fast-twitch muscle fibres are more dependent on the phosphagen and glycogen- lactic acid systems Fast twitch muscle fibres are more dependent on anaerobic metabolism whereas slow-twitch muscle fibres are more dependent on aerobic metabolism. Slow-twitch muscle fibres have more mitochondria, more myoglobin and a higher capillary density. Fast-twitch muscle fibres tend to be larger in diameter as compared to small-twitch muscle fibres.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Most of the energy for strenuous exercise that lasts for more than 5- 10 seconds but less than 1 to 2 minutes comes from which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Anaerobic glycolysis ATP stores and ATP from phosphocreatine can sustain exercise for another the first 5- 10 seconds only. Energy for strenuous exercise for more than 5- 10 seconds but less than 1-2 minutes is derived from anaerobic glycolysis. Release of energy by glycolysis occurs much more rapidly than oxidative release of energy, which is much too slow to supply the needs of the muscle in the first few minutes of exercise.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: The following events occur at an excitatory synapse. A. Ligand- gated channels open in the post synaptic membrane to allow influx of sodium B. Synaptic vesicles bind to pre-synaptic membrane C. Depolarization of pre-synaptic membrane D. Opening of calcium channels cause influx of calcium Which of the following is the correct sequence?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) C, D, B, A Arrival of the action potential at the pre-synaptic membrane, causes opening of calcium channels. This is followed by calcium influx. Vesicles in the pre-synaptic axon terminal bind to the presynaptic membrane. This is followed by exocytosis of the neurotransmitter. The neurotransmitter binds to its receptors on the post synaptic membrane leading to electrical changes in the post- synaptic neuron.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: A 65- year-old man presented with progressive leg weakness and a diagnosis of LEMS (Lambert- Eaton myasthenic syndrome) was made by serial repetitive nerve stimulation test. Which of the following channels are affected in Lamber-Eaton syndrome?

options.label: A
options.text: Voltage- gated calcium channels on pre- synaptic membrane

options.label: B
options.text: Voltage- gated calcium channels on post- synaptic membrane

options.label: C
options.text: Ligand- gated sodium channels on pre- synaptic membrane

options.label: D
options.text: Ligand- gated sodium channels on post- synaptic membrane

questions.answerText: Voltage- gated calcium channels on pre- synaptic membrane
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

Voltage- gated calcium channels on pre- synaptic membrane

 

  • LEMS is caused by an auto-immune attach against voltage-gated calcium channels on the pre-synaptic membrane at the NMJ.
  • It is usually adult- onset and has a similar occurrence in males and females. Proximal muscles of the lower extremities are primarily affected, producing a waddling gait and difficulty in raising arms.
  • Repetitive stimulation of the motor nerve facilitates accumulation of calcium in the nerve terminal and increases acetylcholine release, leading to increase in muscle strength. This is in contrast to myasthenia gravis in which symptoms are exacerbated by repetitive stimulation.
  • About 40% of the patients of LEMS also have cancer, especially small cell cancer of the lung.
  • Patients of LEMS may also have lymphosarcoma, malignant thymoma, cancer of the breast, stomach, colon, prostate, bladder, kidney, or gallbladder.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a motor unit?

options.label: A
options.text: Single Aα motor neuron and all the muscle fibres it supplies

options.label: B
options.text: Single muscle fibre and all the Aα motor neurons supplying it

options.label: C
options.text: Single sensory neuron and all the muscle fibres it supplies

options.label: D
options.text: Single muscle fibre and all the sensory neurons supplying it

questions.answerText: Single Aα motor neuron and all the muscle fibres it supplies
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

Single muscle fibre and all the Aα motor neurons supplying it

Single A alpha motor neuron and all the muscle fibres it innervates constitute a motor unit. The number of muscle fibres in each motor unit varies. In muscles concerned with fine, graded and precise movements, such as those of the hand and those concerned with movements of the eyeball, each motor unit innervates very few (3- 6) muscle fibres. On the other hand, calf muscles may have up to 600 muscle fibres in each motor unit.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stemHtml: Given below is a graph of the length-tension relationship. Which of the following are true regarding optimum length? (multiple correct options).

options.label: A
options.text: Optimum length corresponds to a sarcomere length of 2- 2.2 microns

options.label: B
options.text: There are maximum number of actin- myosin cross bridges at optimum length

options.label: C
options.text: There is minimum overlap between actin and myosin

options.label: D
options.text: Optimum length is also known as the resting length

questions.answerText: Optimum length corresponds to a sarcomere length of 2- 2.2 microns
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A, B, D are correct.) At optimum length, total tension, active tension and passive tension are maximum. Optimum length corresponds to a sarcomere length of 2- 2.2 microns. There is maximum overlap between actin and myosin with maximum number of actin- myosin cross bridges at this length. Optimum length is also known as the resting length.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Each molecule of troponin C can bind how many calcium ions?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) 4 Each molecule of troponin-C can bind strongly with up to 4 calcium ions.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Acetylcholine receptors on the motor end plate are which of the following?

options.label: B
options.text: Voltage gated sodium and potassium channels

options.label: D
options.text: Ligand gated sodium and potassium channels

questions.answerText: Ligand gated sodium and potassium channels
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Ligand gated sodium and potassium channels Acetylcholine receptors on the motor end plate are pentameric ligand gated sodium and potassium channels but the movement of sodium predominates through these channels.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct sequence of events in skeletal muscle?

options.label: A
options.text: Muscle action potential, muscle contraction, nerve action potential

options.label: B
options.text: Nerve action potential, muscle contraction, muscle action potential

options.label: C
options.text: Muscle contraction, nerve action potential, muscle action potential

options.label: D
options.text: Nerve action potential, muscle action potential, muscle contraction

questions.answerText: Nerve action potential, muscle action potential, muscle contraction
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Nerve action potential, muscle action potential, muscle contraction Action potential in a motor neuron causes release of Acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction. Ach diffuses across the synaptic cleft, binds with its receptors on the motor end plate causing opening of ligand gated sodium and potassium channels. As a result of net gain of positive ions the muscle fibre membrane depolarizes. The muscle membrane reaches a threshold potential, causing voltage gated sodium channels to open, and a muscle action potential follows. The muscle action potential leads to contraction of the muscle.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stemHtml: Shown below is an electron microscopic picture of a sarcomere. Which of the following represent the H-zone?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) A is the dark or A (anisotropic to light) band which consists of myosin and overlapped actin. Within the A-band there is lighter area called the H-zone (D), which consists of only myosin. E is the I (isotropic to light) or light band- it consists of only actin.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following is greater in afterloaded muscle contractions as compared to preloaded muscle contractions?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

Latent period.

  • Preload is the load placed on a muscle before the muscle contracts.
  • It serves to stretch the muscle sarcomeres, thus producing a passive tension across the muscle.
  • This passive tension increases muscle contraction in two ways:

                (i) It adds an elastic recoil force to the muscle during its contraction;

                (ii) It stretches the muscle to its resting length, producing the optimum   length-tension relationship for active force generation.

  • In real life situations, it is a common practice to pre-stretch a muscle using antagonist muscles.
  • After load is an opposing force which the muscle encounters immediately after it starts contracting. It is a force that a muscle must overcome before an observable shortening of the muscle can occur.

The contraction and work done of an after-loaded muscle is comparatively lesser.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman visits her physician because of double vision, drooping of eyelids, difficulty in chewing and swallowing, and general weakness in her limbs. All these symptoms worsen with exercise and occur more frequently late in the day. The physician suspects myasthenia gravis and orders a Tensilon test. The test is positive. What is the most likely basis for the symptoms described in this patient?

options.label: A
options.text: Depletion of voltage-gated calcium channels in certain motor neurons

options.label: B
options.text: Development of macro motor units after recovery from poliomyelitis

options.label: C
options.text: Over exertion resulting in junction fatigue

questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies Myasthenia gravis (MG) is a chronic autoimmune disorder in which antibodies destroy the acetylcholine receptors on the motor end plate, resulting in weakness of the skeletal muscles. Myasthenia gravis affects the voluntary muscles of the body, especially those that control the eyes, mouth, throat and limbs. Tensilon (Edrophonium) is a drug that blocks the breakdown of acetylcholine, helping the neurotransmitter acetylcholine activate the muscle. For patients who do not have MG, the drug will do nothing to improve tired muscles. However, for patients with MG, the test is said to be positive when muscle strength improves.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: A 18- year old football player sustained a left tibial fracture. The left lower leg was placed in a cast for 8 weeks. After the cast was removed the left gastrocnemius muscle was found to be significantly smaller in circumference than the right. What is the most likely explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: Decrease in the number of individual muscle fibres in the left gastrocnemius

options.label: B
options.text: Decrease in blood flow to the muscle caused by constriction from the cast

options.label: C
options.text: Temporary reduction in actin and myosin protein synthesis

options.label: D
options.text: Increase in glycolytic activity in the affected muscle

questions.answerText: Temporary reduction in actin and myosin protein synthesis
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Temporary reduction in actin and myosin protein synthesis Skeletal muscle continuously remodels in response to their level of use. When a muscle is inactive for an extended period, the rate of synthesis of contractile proteins in individual muscle fibres decreases resulting in overall reduction in muscle mass. This reversible reduction in muscle mass is called atrophy.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: An apparently healthy 15-year-old boy dies during a minor surgical procedure while under general anesthesia. The boy’s grandfather has also died during a surgical procedure. A clinical assessment team determines that the child had malignant hyperthermia (MH). MH is an inherited disease in which the triggering agents, such as certain anesthetics, stimulate calcium release from storage sites in muscle, leading to elevated concentration of sarcoplasmic calcium. The MH crisis is most likely to be associated with which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Defective ryanodine receptors In malignant hyperthermia, defective ryanodine receptors respond to anesthetics such as, halothane, ether, etc., by opening the calcium channels on the sarcoplasmic reticulum causing uncontrolled release of calcium and thus, increasing the sarcoplasmic calcium. This increase in sarcoplasmic calcium results in continuous contraction of the muscles. This in turn results in increase in body temperature, increased anerobic metabolism, increased CO2 production, and increased lactic acid production. Calsequestrin is a calcium binding protein present in sarcoplasmic reticulum of muscle fibres and is not affected by halothane or halogenated anesthetics. DHPR present on the T-tubule membrane are voltage sensors and are activated by the skeletal muscle fibre action potential and are not affected by halogenated anesthetics.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following is responsible for elasticity in skeletal muscle?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Titin Titin is responsible for muscle elasticity. Titin binds the Z- line to the M-line. The titin molecules act as a framework that holds the myosin and actin filaments in place so that the contractile machinery of the sarcomere will work.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: During a graded activity which of the following is true?

options.label: A
options.text: Fast muscle fibres are recruited before slow muscle fibres

options.label: B
options.text: Large muscle fibres are recruited before small muscle fibres

options.label: C
options.text: Well perfused muscle fibres are recruited before poorly perfused muscle fibres

options.label: D
options.text: Strong muscle fibres are recruited before weak muscle fibres

questions.answerText: Well perfused muscle fibres are recruited before poorly perfused muscle fibres
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Well perfused muscle fibres are recruited before poorly perfused muscle fibres As per the size principle, type 1 muscle fibres are recruited before type 2 muscle fibres. Type 1 muscle fibres are slow, small diameter fibres, with oxidative metabolism. They are red in appearance, well perfused with high capillary density, more mitochondria and more myoglobin as compared to the type 2 fibres. Type 2 fibres are fast, large diameter fibres, with glycolytic metabolism. These are white in appearance.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Resting length corresponds with a which of the following sarcomere lengths?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) 2 µ During an isometric contraction, maximum strength of contraction and maximum tension occurs when the initial length of sarcomere is 2.0 to 2.2 µ. This initial

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stemHtml: Given below is the myogram of a single muscle twitch. What is the tetanizing frequency?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) 40-49 Hz Tetanizing frequency is 1/contraction period (seconds). Here the contraction period is 22milliseconds or 22/1000 second. Tetanizing frequency will, therefore, be 1000/22 per second or 40- 49 Hz.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: A 50-year old woman was admitted to the hospital with symptoms of nausea and vomiting for about 2 days followed by severe muscle weakness and neurologic symptoms, including ptosis and dysphagia. She gave a history of having eaten at a restaurant the evening before the symptoms began. Laboratory tests were positive for Clostridium botulinum. The basis for the muscle weakness in this case was most likely because the toxin

options.label: A
options.text: Blocked the reuptake of neurotransmitter into pre-synaptic terminals

options.label: B
options.text: Bound irreversibly to the receptors on the post-synaptic membrane

options.label: C
options.text: Prevented release of acetylcholine from motor neurons

options.label: D
options.text: Reached the cell body of the motor neuron by diffusion into the spinal cord

questions.answerText: Prevented release of acetylcholine from motor neurons
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Prevented release of acetylcholine from motor neurons Botulinum toxin inactivates the docking proteins in terminals of motor neurons preventing the release of acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junctions.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: All of the following are sarcolemmal proteins except
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Perlecan Perlecan (PLC) also known as basement membrane-specific heparan sulfate proteoglycan core protein (HSPG) or heparan sulfate proteoglycan 2 (HSPG2), is a protein that in humans is encoded by the HSPG2 gene. Perlecan was originally isolated from a basement membrane-producing tumor, the Engelbreth–Holm–Swarm tumor.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following is produced type of heat is produced only in a muscle contracting isotonically?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Relaxation heat Resting heat, initial heat (activation and shortening heat), recovery heat are generated during both in isotonic and isometric muscle contractions. If a muscle that has contracted isotonically is restored to its previous length, extra heat in addition to recovery heat is produced and this is k/a relaxation heat. External work must be done on the muscle to return it to its previous length, and relaxation heat is mainly a manifestation of this work.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: Which of the following is associated with mutation of the genes coding for sarcoglycans?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Limb girdle dystrophy Duchenne’s muscular dystrophy is a serious form of dystrophy in which the dystrophin protein is absent from muscle. It is a X-linked disorder and usually fatal by the age of 30. Becker muscular dystrophy is a milder form of the disease where dystrophin is present but reduced in amount. Tibialis muscular dystrophy is a genetic muscle disease of titin that destabilizes the folded state of the protein.

questions.topic: DAMS · Physiology-Renal Physiology Skeletal muscle-Special First Year Class Test
questions.stem: All of the following are features of complete tetanus except?

options.label: A
options.text: There is no relaxation between successive contractions

options.label: B
options.text: There are periods of incomplete relaxation between successive contractions

options.label: C
options.text: Tension developed during a complete tetanus is about four times that developed by individual twitch contractions

options.label: D
options.text: Stimulation frequency at which summation of contractions occurs producing complete tetanus is determined by the contraction period of that particular muscle

questions.answerText: There are periods of incomplete relaxation between successive contractions
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) There are periods of incomplete relaxation between successive contractions In incomplete tetanus there are periods of incomplete relaxation between successive contractions.
